title: Hekatompedon temple

references.observation: Sioumpara’s study of the stone fragments supports a peripteral Doric temple about 24 × 47 × 14 m and reconstructs 4.06 m front and 3.95 m side bays. The proposed southwest location lies under the later Parthenon podium.
The Archaic Parthenon probably corresponds to the Hekatompedon. The distinct Old Temple of Athena Polias is identified separately beside the Erechtheion.
The poros flank capital records the top of the fluted column, three rings, curved echinus and square abacus.

The three surviving groups comprise lions attacking a bull, Herakles wrestling Triton and the three-bodied figure with connected serpent tails. The relief uses ochre, red, dark blue and black pigments. The crown includes poros cornice and marble gutter.
Reference photograph of a lioness with a mane attacking its calf. The displayed part measures 1.6 × 3.22 m. The surviving composition supplies the east gable center.
Photograph shows a row of three bearded torsos, painted hair and wrapped multicolored tails, with symbols held in the hands.

limitations: The location follows one published interpretation. The original temple foundations are unexposed and the precise anchor, original rotation, ancient terrace elevation and stair profiles are uncertain.

The 6 × 12 peristyle fits the published end and flank bay spacing and temple envelope. Column height, interior plan, roof pitch, paint distribution, roof ornaments and unpreserved figures are interpretations.
The reliefs are original modeled interpretations of the surviving groups. No museum mesh or photographic texture is embedded. The selected year represents the finished Archaic temple.
